div.head: PREFACE.
div.p: In 1897 the present publishers issued in Norwegian an Explanation of Luther's Small Catechism by Pastor H. U. Sverdrup, being an abridged edition of a larger work by the same author, based on Dr. Pontoppidan's Explanation of the Catechism. Some alterations were made in the answers to questions 244–252. The present work is a translation of this abridged and slightly altered edition.

A literal translation has been avoided rather than sought; an attempt has been made to render the original in the simplest and strongest English, and to avoid words and expressions with which the young are little familiar.

In the catechism proper the Standard English Catechism Version has been followed when it did not interfere with the plan stated above. But departures have been made reluctantly and only when simplicity and clearness seemed to be gained thereby. It is not thought that these few changes will cause any disturbance.
Scripture quotations have been added somewhat freely from the larger edition.
As the needs of our English speaking young people have been constantly borne in mind during the preparation of this translation, it is hoped that the book may not fail to carry some blessing to them.
October, 1900.

p.hi: The Translator.

div.head: THE FIRST COMMANDMENT.

p.hi: Thou shalt have no other gods before me.

div.p: That is,
We should fear, love, and trust in God above all things.

div.head: THE SECOND COMMANDMENT.

p.hi: Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain; for the Lord will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain.

div.p: That is,
We should fear and love God, and not curse, swear, conjure, lie, or deceive by His name, but call upon His name in every time of need, and worship Him with prayer, praise, and thanksgiving.

div.head: THE THIRD COMMANDMENT.

p.hi: Remember the Sabbath day to keep it holy.

div.p: That is,
We should fear and love God, and not despise or neglect His Word, but deem it holy and gladly hear and learn it.

div.head: THE FOURTH COMMANDMENT.

p.hi: Honor thy father and thy mother, that it may be well with thee, and thou mayest live long on the earth.

div.p: That is,
We should fear and love God, and not despise or give offense to our parents or superiors; but honor, serve, obey, love, and esteem them.

div.head: THE FIFTH COMMANDMENT.

p.hi: Thou shalt not kill.

div.p: That is,
We should fear and love God, and not hurt or harm our neighbor in his body, but help and befriend him in all bodily distress.

div.head: THE SIXTH COMMANDMENT.

p.hi: Thou shalt not commit adultery.

div.p: That is,
We should fear and love God, and live a chaste and pure life, in words and deeds, husband and wife loving and honoring each other.

div.head: THE SEVENTH COMMANDMENT.

p.hi: Thou shalt not steal.

div.p: That is,
We should fear and love God, and not take our neighbor's money or property, nor get it by unfair dealing or other dishonesty, but help him to improve and protect his property and living.

div.head: THE EIGHTH COMMANDMENT.

p.hi: Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbor.

div.p: That is,
We should fear and love God, and not tell lies about our neighbor, nor betray, slander, or defame him; but excuse him, speak well of him, and look upon all his acts as well-meant.

div.head: THE NINTH COMMANDMENT.

p.hi: Thou shalt not covet thy neighbor's house.

div.p: That is,
We should fear and love God, and not by deceit or craft seek to gain our neighbor's inheritance or home, nor try to get it though we seem to have some right thereto, but help him to keep his own.

div.head: THE TENTH COMMANDMENT.

p.hi: Thou shalt not covet thy neighbor's wife, nor his man-servant, nor his maid-servant, nor his cattle, nor anything that is his.

div.p: That is,
We should fear and love God, and not estrange, force, or entice away from our neighbor, his wife, servants, or cattle, but urge them to stay and do their duty.

p.hi: What does God say of all his commandments?

I the Lord thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me; and showing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments.

div.p: That is,
God threatens to punish all who transgress these commandments; we should therefore fear His wrath, and do nothing against them.
On the other hand He promises grace and every blessing to all who keep these commandments; we should therefore love Him and trust in Him, and gladly do according to His commandments.

div.head: THE THREE ARTICLES OF THE CREED.
CONCERNING CREATION.

p.hi: I believe in God the Father Almighty, Maker of heaven and earth.

div.p: That is,
I believe that God has made me and all other creatures; that He has given me body and soul, eyes, ears, and all other members, my reason, and all my senses.
I also believe that He preserves all He has made, and that He daily provides me with all I need, giving me clothing and food, home and family, and every good thing.
I further believe that He protects me from all danger, and keeps me from all evil; not because I have deserved it, but because He is a loving and merciful Father.
For all these blessings it is my duty to serve Him thankfully and obediently all the days of my life.
All this is certainly true.

div.head: CONCERNING REDEMPTION.

p.hi: I believe in Jesus Christ His only Son, our Lord; who was conceived by the Holy Ghost, born of the Virgin Mary; suffered under Pontius Pilate, was crucified, dead, and buried; He descended into hell; the third day He arose again from the dead; He ascended into heaven, and sitteth on the right hand of God the Father Almighty; from whence He shall come to judge the quick and the dead.

div.p: That is,

I believe that Jesus Christ is true God, begotten of the Father from eternity; I also believe that He is true man, born of the Virgin Mary; that He is my Lord, who has redeemed me, a lost and condemned sinner; who has freed me from sin, from death, and from the power of Satan, not with gold or silver but with His holy and precious blood and His innocent death.

All this He has done that I might be His own, and that I might serve Him in righteousness, innocence, and happiness, and live and reign with Him in His kingdom forever, even as He arose from the dead, lives and reigns through all eternity.
All this is certainly true.

div.head: CONCERNING SANCTIFICATION.

p.hi: I believe in the Holy Ghost; the holy Christian church, the communion of saints; the forgiveness of sins; the resurrection of the body; and life everlasting. Amen.

div.p: That is,

I believe that I cannot through my own strength believe in Jesus Christ my Lord, or come to Him. This is the work of the Holy Spirit alone, who has called me through the gospel, enlightened me with His gifts, and sanctified and preserved me in the true faith;
Even as he calls, gathers, enlightens, and sanctifies the whole Christian church on earth, and preserves it in fellowship with Jesus Christ in the one true faith.
In this Christian church He daily forgives me and all believers all our sins, and He will raise up me and all the dead on the last day, and will give me and all believers everlasting life.
All this is certainly true.

div.head: THE LORD'S PRAYER.

p.hi: Our Father who art in heaven.

div.p: That is,

God would hereby tenderly invite us to believe that He is truly our Father, and we are truly His children, so that we may ask of Him with all cheerfulness and confidence, as dear children ask of their dear father.

div.head: THE FIRST PETITION.

p.hi: Hallowed be Thy name.

div.p: That is,
The name of God is indeed holy in itself; but we pray in this petition that it may be hallowed also among us.
This is done when the Word of God is rightly taught, and when we as the children of God live holy lives in obedience to the Word. This grant us, heavenly Father.

div.head: THE SECOND PETITION.

p.hi: Thy kingdom come.

div.p: That is,
The kingdom of God comes indeed of itself, without our prayer, but we pray in this petition that it may come also to us.
This is done when our heavenly Father gives us His Holy Spirit, so that by His grace we believe the Word of God, and live holy and Christ-like lives here in time, and in heaven forever.

div.head: THE THIRD PETITION.

p.hi: Thy will be done on earth, as it is in heaven.

div.p: That is,
The good and gracious will of God is done indeed without our prayer; but we pray in this petition that it may be done also among us.
This is done when God brings to nothing all evil plans and purposes of the devil, the world, and our own flesh, that would hinder the hallowing of His name and the coming of His kingdom.
On the other hand, it is the good and gracious will of God to strengthen us and keep us steadfast in His Word and in faith, until death.

div.head: THE FOURTH PETITION.

p.hi: Give us this day our daily bread.

div.p: That is,

God gives daily bread indeed without our prayer even to the wicked; but we pray in this petition that He would help us to appreciate His benefits, that we may receive our daily bread with thanksgiving.

By daily bread is meant all those things which are needed for our support and well-being in life, as food and clothing, home and property, happy family relations, a good government, favorable weather, peace and health, faithful friends, good neighbors, and the like.

div.head: THE FIFTH PETITION.

p.hi: And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

div.p: That is,

We pray in this petition that our Father in heaven would not look upon our sins, nor, on account of them, deny our prayer, for we are not worthy of anything we ask, neither have we deserved it; but we pray that He would give it to us out of His mercy; for we sin every day, and deserve nothing but punishment.
And we on our part will heartily forgive those who have sinned against us, and return good for evil.

div.head: THE SIXTH PETITION.

p.hi: And lead us not into temptation.

div.p: That is,

God indeed tempts no one, but we pray in this petition that He would guard and keep us from the devil, the world, and our own flesh, that we fall not, through their deceit, into unbelief, despair, or other sins; but we pray that although we be thus tempted, we may overcome the temptation, and remain victorious.

div.head: THE SEVENTH PETITION.

p.hi: But deliver us from evil.

div.p: That is,

We pray in this petition, in general, that our Father in heaven would deliver us from all evil, affecting body and soul, property and honor, and at last grant us a blessed end, and graciously take us from this world of sorrow to Himself in heaven.

p.hi: What are the closing words of the Lord's Prayer?
For Thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever and ever. Amen.

div.p: That is,
We should remember that God is able to answer our prayer, and that the glory belongs to Him alone, when we get according to our prayer.

p.hi: Why is the word "Amen" added?

div.p: It is added in order that I may be fully assured that these petitions are acceptable to our Father in heaven, and are heard by Him.

div.head: THE SACRAMENT OF BAPTISM.

p.hi: What is Baptism?

div.p: Baptism is not water alone, but it is water comprehended in God's command, and united with His Word.

p.hi: What is God's command concerning Baptism?

div.p: It is given in the words of Christ in the last chapter of Matthew:

p.hi: "Go ye, therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost."
What benefit do we have from Baptism?

div.p: Baptism works the forgiveness of sins, delivers from death and the devil, and gives everlasting life to all who believe what the Word and promises of God declare.

p.hi: What is God's promise concerning Baptism?

div.p: It is given in the words of Christ in the sixteenth chapter of Mark:

p.hi: "He that believeth and is baptized shall be saved; but he that believeth not shall be condemned."
How can water do such great things?

div.p: It is not water indeed that does it, but the Word of God, which is in and with the water, and faith which trusts this Word of God in the water.

For without the Word of God, the water is water alone, and no Baptism. But with the Word of God it is a Baptism, that is, a gracious water of life and a washing of regeneration in the Holy Ghost; as Paul says in the third chapter of the epistle to Titus:

"According to His mercy He saved us, by the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Holy Ghost; which He shed on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Savior; that being justified by His grace, we should be made heirs according to the hope of eternal life."

p.hi: What does the baptizing with water signify?

div.p: It signifies that the old man in us should, by daily sorrow and repentance, be drowned and die, with all sins and evil desires; and again a new man daily appear more and more, who shall live before God in righteousness and purity forever.

div.head: THE SACRAMENT OF THE LORD'S SUPPER.

p.hi: What is the Lord's Supper?

div.p: It is the true body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, under bread and wine, instituted by Christ Himself for Christians to eat and to drink.

p.hi: Repeat the Words of Institution.

"Our Lord Jesus Christ, in the night in which He was betrayed, took bread, and when He had given thanks, He brake it and gave it to His disciples, saying, Take, eat; this is my body, which is given for you; this do in remembrance of me.

"After the same manner, also, when He had supped, He took the cup, and when He had given thanks, He gave it to them, saying, Drink ye all of it; this cup is the New Testament in my blood, which is shed for you, and for many, for the remission of sins; this do, as oft as ye drink it, in remembrance of me."
What benefit do we have from the Lord's Supper?

div.p: It is shown by these words: "Given and shed for you, for the remission of sins;" namely, that in the sacrament forgiveness of sins, life, and salvation are given us through these words. For where there is forgiveness of sins, there is also life and salvation.

p.hi: How can bodily eating and drinking do such great things?

div.p: It is not the eating and drinking, indeed, that does it, but the words which stand here: "Given and shed for you, for the remission of sins." These words, together with the bodily eating and drinking, are the chief thing in the sacrament; and He that believes these words, has what they say and mean, namely, the forgiveness of sins.

p.hi: Who, then, receive this sacrament worthily?

div.p: Fasting and bodily preparation are indeed a good outward practise;
But he alone is truly worthy and well prepared, who believes these words: "Given and shed for you, for the remission of sins."
But he who believes not these words is unworthy and unprepared. The words, "for you" require truly believing hearts.

div.head: INTRODUCTION.

p.hi: 1. What is God's will concerning man?

div.p: God willeth that all men should be saved, and come to the knowledge of the truth. 1 Tim. 2:4.

p.hi: 2. Where does God show us how we may be saved?

div.p: In the holy Scriptures, also called the Bible.

p.hi: 3. Who wrote the Bible?

div.p: The holy prophets, evangelists, and apostles wrote the Bible.

p.hi: 4. But how can their word be the Word of God?

div.p: The Spirit of God revealed to them what to speak and write.

p.hi: 2 Pet. 1:21. [R. V.] Men spoke from God, being moved by the Holy Ghost.
2 Tim. 3:16. All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness.
5. What must we do to experience personally that their word is the Word of God?

div.p: We must obey the Word and receive it into our hearts.

p.hi: John 7:17. If any man will do his will, he shall know of the doctrine, whether it be of God, or whether I speak of myself.
6. Is the Bible then the only safe rule of our faith and duty?

div.p: Yes; the Bible alone contains full information of the will of God concerning our salvation.

p.hi: 7. How do we rightly use the Word of God?

div.p: We must first look to God for the light of His Spirit, and then read with devotion and an earnest purpose to live according to the Word.

p.hi: 1 Cor. 2:14. [R. V.] The natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God: for they are foolishness unto him; and he cannot know them, because they are spiritually judged.
8. Who should read the Bible?

div.p: It is the will of God that all should use His Word and love it as a dear gift.

p.hi: 9. What is the substance of all the books of the Bible?

div.p: The great truth that Jesus is the way to salvation for all who believe.

p.hi: John 20:31. But these are written, that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God; and that believing ye might have life through his name.
10. How is the Bible divided in regard to its teaching?

div.p: It is divided into Law and Gospel.

p.hi: 11. What is the Law?

div.p: The Law is the divine Word which tells us what we must do.

p.hi: 12. What is the Gospel?

div.p: The Gospel is the glad tidings of the grace of God in Jesus Christ our Savior.

div.head: THE TEN COMMANDMENTS, OR THE LAW.

p.hi: 13. How has God given His law to us?

div.p: 1. In the creation God wrote His Law in the heart of man. (Conscience.) Rom. 2:15.
2. At Mount Sinai He gave His Law in the Ten Commandments, written on two tables of stone. Ex. 20:1–17.

p.hi: 14. Does this Law demand outward observance only?

div.p: No; it demands the whole man, and the willing obedience of heart and mind.

p.hi: Luk. 10:27. Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy strength, and with all thy mind.
15. Can we be saved through the Law?

div.p: No; since the fall in sin no man can perfectly keep the Law.

p.hi: Rom. 8:7. The carnal mind is enmity against God: for it is not subject to the law of God, neither indeed can it be.
16. Of what benefit, then, is the Law?

div.p: 1. It points out to us our sins and the wrath of God toward sin.

p.hi: Rom. 3:20. [R. V.] Through the law cometh the knowledge of sin.

div.p: 2. It makes us anxious to seek Christ.

p.hi: Gal. 3:24. The law was our schoolmaster to bring us to Christ.

div.p: 3. It points out to the believer what fruits his faith must bear.

p.hi: Ps. 119:105. Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.
17. What is the substance of the law?

div.p: Love to God, ourselves, and our neighbor. Matt. 22:37–40.

p.hi: Rom. 13:10. [R. V.] Love is the fulfilment of the law.
1 Tim. 1:5. [R. V.] But the end of the charge is love out of a pure heart and a good conscience and faith unfeigned.

div.head: THE FIRST TABLE OF THE LAW.

p.hi: 18. What is the substance of the first table?

div.p: Love of God.

p.hi: Luk 10:27. Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy strength, and with all thy mind.

div.head: THE FIRST COMMANDMENT.

p.hi: Thou shalt have no other gods before me.

div.p: That is,
We should fear, love, and trust in God above all things.

p.hi: 19. What does the first commandment forbid?

div.p: It forbids the worship of strange gods, or idols.

p.hi: Matt. 4:10. Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve.
20. What is meant by an idol?

div.p: Anything that man worships, fears, loves, and trusts in instead of the one true God.

p.hi: 21. Who practice idolatry openly?

div.p: They who worship the created things instead of the Creator, and pray to the sun, the moon, stars, images, angels, or saints.

p.hi: Rom. 1:25. They changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed forever.
22. Who practice idolatry secretly?

div.p: They who turn their love, fear, and trust from the living God, that they may secretly cling to something else than Him.

p.hi: 23. Whom do all idolaters really serve?

div.p: They serve the devil who is the father of lies, and the lord of all impenitent and hardened sinners.

p.hi: 1 John 3:8. [R. V.] He that doeth sin is of the devil.
2 Cor. 4:4. [R. V.] The god of this world hath blinded the minds of the unbelieving.
24. What does God require of us in the first commandment?

div.p: We should fear, love, and trust in God above all things.

p.hi: 25. Upon what does God then really look?

div.p: Upon the attitude of our hearts toward Him.

p.hi: Prov. 23:26. My son, give me thine heart.
Prov. 4:23. Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life.
26. When do we fear God?

div.p: We fear God when we think so highly of Him, that we are afraid of offending Him by any wrongdoing.

p.hi: Ps. 33:8. Let all the earth fear the Lord!
27. Of how many kinds is the fear of God?

div.p: Of two kinds: slavish fear and child-like fear.

p.hi: 28. What is meant by slavish fear?

div.p: When we fear God because we are afraid of punishment.

p.hi: 29. What is meant by child-like fear?

div.p: When we love God so dearly that we wish to do nothing that is against His will.

p.hi: Gen. 39:9. How then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?
1 John 4:18. Perfect love casteth out fear.
30. Who fear God in this manner?

div.p: God's children only.

p.hi: Rom. 8:15. [R. V.] Ye received not the spirit of bondage again unto fear; but ye received the spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father.
31. When do we love God?

div.p: We love God when He is dearer to us than all else, so that we have no true joy except in Him, and gladly submit to His will in all things.

p.hi: Ps. 18:1. I will love Thee, O Lord, my strength.
Ps. 73:25, 26. Whom have I in heaven but Thee? and there is none upon earth that I desire beside Thee. My flesh and my heart faileth: but God is the strength of my heart, and my portion forever.
32. Can we love God and the world at the same time?

div.p: By no means.

p.hi: Matt. 6:24. No man can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.
1 John. 2:15. Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world. If any man love the world, the love of the Father is not in him.
33. Why must we love God?

div.p: We must love God because of His goodness toward us.

p.hi: Matt. 19:17. There is none good but one, that is God.
1 John 4:19. We love him, because He first loved us.
34. Whereby is it seen that we love God?

div.p: By a holy life.

p.hi: John 14:21. He that hath my commandments and keepeth them, he it is that loveth me.
35. When do we trust in God above all things?

div.p: We trust in God above all things when we have confidence in Him as in a loving father, and when we look to Him for every blessing, and put all our affairs into His hands.

p.hi: 1 Pet. 5:7. Casting all your anxiety upon him, because he careth for you.
Ps. 37:5. Commit thy way unto the Lord; trust also in Him; and He shall bring it to pass.
36. Why must we trust in God alone?

div.p: Because He is our almighty and faithful Friend.

p.hi: 37. Name some virtues that follow upon true fear, love, and trust in God.

div.p: Humility, patience, and self-denial.

p.hi: 1 Pet. 5:5, 6. God resisteth the proud and giveth grace to the humble. Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God, that He may exalt you in due time.
Job 1:21. The Lord gave, and the Lord hath taken away; blessed be the name of the Lord!
Matt. 26:39. Not as I will, but as Thou wilt.

div.head: THE SECOND COMMANDMENT.

p.hi: Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain: for the Lord will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain.

div.p: That is,
We should fear and love God, and not curse, swear, conjure, lie, or deceive by His name, but call upon His name in every time of need, and worship Him with prayer, praise, and thanksgiving.

p.hi: 38. What is meant by the "name" of God?

div.p: 1. The usual names given to Him in the Bible.
2. His nature and attributes and all that by which He is especially known, such as His Word, sacraments, and works.

p.hi: 39. When is the name of God taken in vain?

div.p: When it is used in a thoughtless and mocking manner and without devotion and reverence.

p.hi: 40. How is this done?

div.p: 1. When we use God's name or Word in jesting or as a by-word.
2. When we find fault with anything God has done.
3. When we use the name of God in cursing, swearing, conjuring, lying, or deceiving.

p.hi: 41. What is it to curse by the name of God?

div.p: It is to call down evil upon ourselves, our neighbor, or any other created thing, by the name of God.

p.hi: 42. What is it to swear by the name of God?

div.p: It is to bear witness to anything by the holy name of God.

p.hi: 43. Are we never permitted to swear?

div.p: Yes; when the proper authorities demand it in God's stead.

p.hi: 44. Why is it a great sin to commit perjury?

div.p: Because the perjurer shows open disregard for God and the salvation of his own soul, and frankly calls down the judgment of God upon himself.

p.hi: 45. Are cursing and swearing sinful when the name of God is not used?

div.p: Yes, indeed; for whatever we curse or swear by, we really do so by God who is the Lord of all things.

p.hi: Matt. 5:34–37. Swear not at all; neither by heaven; for it is God's throne:
Nor by the earth; for it is his footstool: neither by Jerusalem; for it is the city of the great King.
Neither shalt thou swear by thy head, because thou canst not make one hair white or black.
But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.
46. Are cursing and swearing sinful when they have become a habit?

div.p: Most certainly; for a sinful habit proves that sin is our master.

p.hi: 47. What is it to conjure by the name of God?

div.p: It is trying to cure diseases, or to practice any other kind of superstition, by the name of God or a passage from the Bible.

p.hi: 48. How do we lie and deceive by the name of God?

div.p: By perjury, false teaching, and hypocrisy.

p.hi: Matt. 15:9. In vain they do worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men.
Titus 1:16. They profess that they know God; but by their works they deny Him.
49. What must he expect who takes the name of God in vain?

div.p: Great punishment, both in time and eternity; for the Lord will not hold him guiltless that taketh His name in vain.

p.hi: 50. How do we use the name of God properly?

div.p: When we sincerely call upon the name of God in every time of need, and worship Him with prayer, praise, and thanksgiving.

div.head: THE THIRD COMMANDMENT.

p.hi: Remember the Sabbath day to keep it holy.

div.p: That is,
We should fear and love God, and not despise or neglect His Word, but deem it holy and gladly hear and learn it.

p.hi: 51. Which day is the day of rest among Christians?

div.p: Sunday, the first day of the week, on which Christ arose from the dead.

p.hi: 52. How should we keep the day of rest holy?

div.p: 1. We must rest from our daily labor, that the time may be used for our instruction in the fear of the Lord.
2. We must earnestly hear and study the Word of God, both in our homes and in church.

p.hi: Luke 11:28. Blessed are they that hear the Word of God, and keep it.
James 1:27. Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world.
53. Has the Lord appointed these resting-days to be used only in reading and studying the Word of God?

div.p: No; He has appointed such days also for the needed rest of mind and body.

p.hi: 54. How do we misuse the day of rest?

div.p: 1. When we neglect and despise the Word of God.

p.hi: Eccl. 5:1. Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God.

div.p: 2. When we do work or take part in amusements that either are actually sinful or turn our minds away from God.

p.hi: 55. Is no work permitted on Sunday?

div.p: Yes; any work of necessity that cannot be delayed, and any loving kindness we may show our neighbor who is in need. Luk. 14:1–6.

div.head: THE SECOND TABLE OF THE LAW.

p.hi: 56. What is the substance of the second table?

div.p: Love to ourselves and our neighbor.

p.hi: Matt. 22:39. Thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself.
57. May we love ourselves?

div.p: Yes, for God has made us, but we must beware of selfishness.

p.hi: 58. What should a man care for most of all?

div.p: For his soul, the immortal part of himself.

p.hi: Matt. 16:26. For what is a man profited, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?
59. What does the second table teach us about our relation to our neighbor?

div.p: We must feel and act toward him, as we would have him feel and act toward us.

p.hi: Matt. 7:12. All things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them.
1 John 3:18. Let us not love in word, neither with the tongue: but in deed and truth.
60. Who is our neighbor?

div.p: Every human being is our neighbor. Read Luke 10:29–37.

p.hi: 61. Must we love also our enemies?

div.p: Yes; for even our enemy is our neighbor.

p.hi: Matt. 5:44, 45. Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you;
That ye may be the children of your Father which is in heaven.

div.head: THE FOURTH COMMANDMENT.

p.hi: Honor thy father and thy mother, that it may be well with thee, and thou mayest live long on the earth.

div.p: That is,
We should fear and love God, and not despise or give offense to our parents or superiors; but honor, serve, obey, love, and esteem them.

p.hi: 62. Why must we honor father and mother?

div.p: Because God has placed them over us to care for us.

p.hi: Lev. 19:3. Ye shall fear every man his mother and his father: I am the Lord your God.
63. How are children to show that they honor father and mother?

div.p: By respectful, loving, and willing obedience and by good behavior to their parents, both in their presence and in their absence.

p.hi: Prov. 1:8. My son, hear the instruction of thy father, and forsake not the law of thy mother.
Eph. 6:1. Children, obey your parents in the Lord: for this is right.
64. Whom must we honor and obey besides our parents?

div.p: All those whom God has placed over us, such as guardians, employers, teachers, and the government.

p.hi: 65. Must we obey parents and superiors when they ask us to do what is sinful?

div.p: No; we ought to obey God rather than men. Acts 5:29.

p.hi: 66. What is the duty of parents toward their children?

div.p: They must love them, pray for them, bring them up in the fear of the Lord, and in everything seek their temporal and spiritual good.

p.hi: Prov. 13:24. He that spareth his rod hateth his son: but he that loveth him chasteneth him betimes.
67. What is God's promise to those who honor father and mother?

div.p: It shall be well with them, and they shall live long on the earth.

p.hi: 68. Is this promise yet effective?

div.p: Yes; in this sense, that special blessings rest upon obedient children, and upon every nation honoring father and mother.

p.hi: 69. Has God given us also a land?

div.p: Yes; He has given us our native land, that we may love it and help it to prosper.

p.hi: 70. What does the fourth commandment forbid?

div.p: To despise and give offense to father and mother.

p.hi: Prov. 17:25. A foolish son is a grief to his father, and bitterness to her that bare him.
71. What does he bring upon himself who transgresses this commandment?

div.p: Condemnation and punishment from God.

p.hi: Deut. 27:16. Cursed be he that setteth light by his father or his mother.

div.head: THE FIFTH COMMANDMENT.

p.hi: Thou shalt not kill.

div.p: That is,
We should fear and love God, and not hurt or harm our neighbor in his body, but help and befriend him in all bodily distress.

p.hi: 72. How is this commandment transgressed?

div.p: 1. By taking our neighbor's life, or by doing him any bodily harm.

p.hi: Gen. 9:6. Whoso sheddeth man's blood, by man shall his blood be shed: for in the image of God made he man.

div.p: 2. By hatred, anger, abusive words, and all offensive behavior toward our neighbor.

p.hi: 1 John 3:15. Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer: and ye know that no murderer hath eternal life abiding in him.
Eph. 4:31. Let all bitterness, and wrath, and anger, and clamor, and evil speaking, be put away from you, with all malice.
73. Can we kill also our neighbor's soul?

div.p: Yes; when we cause him to sin, either by purposely leading him astray, or by bad example, thus helping to destroy his soul.

p.hi: Rom. 16:18. By good words and fair speeches they deceive the hearts of the simple.
Matt. 18:7. Woe to that man by whom the offense cometh.
74. May we take our own life?

div.p: No; God has given us life, and He alone has the right to take it.

p.hi: 75. What does God require of us in the fifth commandment?

div.p: That we help our neighbor in all bodily distress, and associate with him in love and gentleness.

p.hi: Eph. 4:32. And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ's sake hath forgiven you.
Matt. 25:35, 36. I was hungry, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in;
Naked, and ye clothed me: I was sick, and ye visited me: I was in prison, and ye came unto me.

div.head: THE SIXTH COMMANDMENT.

p.hi: Thou shalt not commit adultery.

div.p: That is,
We should fear and love God, and live a chaste and pure life, in words and deeds, husband and wife loving and honoring each other.

p.hi: 76. How is this commandment transgressed?

div.p: 1. When husband and wife are unfaithful to each other.

p.hi: Heb. 13:4. [R. V.] Let marriage be had in honor among all.

div.p: 2. By all impure thoughts, desires, words, and acts, in married as well as in unmarried persons.

p.hi: Eph. 5:3. But fornication, and all uncleanness, or covetousness, let it not be once named among you, as becometh saints.
77. Who has instituted marriage?

div.p: God Himself instituted it in Paradise.

p.hi: 78. How do unfaithful husbands and wives treat this holy institution?

div.p: They despise it, and thus bring down upon themselves the judgment of God.

p.hi: Heb. 13:4. Whoremongers and adulterers God will judge.
79. Repeat some passages from Scripture in which impurity is forbidden?

div.p: Be not deceived: neither fornicators, nor adulterers, nor effeminate, nor abusers of themselves with mankind, shall inherit the kingdom of God. 1 Cor. 6:9, 10.
Jesus says: I say unto you, that whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart. Matt. 5:28.
Let no corrupt communication proceed out of your mouth! Eph. 4:29.

p.hi: 80. Why is this sin so fearful?

div.p: Because it affects both soul and body more than any other sin.

p.hi: 81. How can we be kept pure?

div.p: We must watch and pray, and avoid everything that awakens impure desires.

p.hi: Matt. 26:41. Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation.
82. What things awaken impure desires?

div.p: Gluttony and drunkenness, immoral and exciting amusements, bad company, the reading of improper books, and everything that excites carnal and impure thoughts.

p.hi: 83. Are not gluttony and drunkenness alone dangerous sins?

div.p: Yes, indeed; they are a shameful abuse of God's gifts, by which we ruin soul and body and shut ourselves out from the kingdom of God.

p.hi: Luk. 21:34. And take heed to yourselves, lest at any time your hearts be overcharged with gluttony, and drunkenness, and cares of this life, and so that day come upon you unawares.
84. What does God require of us in the sixth commandment?

div.p: We must live a chaste and pure life, whether we are married or unmarried, husband and wife loving and honoring each other.

div.head: THE SEVENTH COMMANDMENT.

p.hi: Thou shalt not steal.

div.p: That is,
We should fear and love God, and not take our neighbor's money or property, nor get it by unfair dealing or other dishonesty, but help him to improve and protect his property and living.

p.hi: 85. What is it to steal?

div.p: To steal is to take from our neighbor even the smallest part of his property against his will.

p.hi: 86. How is stealing done?

div.p: In a coarse or in an artful manner.

p.hi: 87. Who steal in a coarse manner?

div.p: Those who, without any right or permission whatever, take their neighbor's money or property.

p.hi: Eph. 4:28. Let him that stole steal no more.
88. Who steal in an artful manner?

div.p: Those who take or withhold the property of others by any kind of fraud.

p.hi: 89. Is it wrong to be a partner with a thief?

div.p: Yes; the partner of a thief is no better than the thief.

p.hi: Prov. 29:24. Whoso is partner with a thief hateth his own soul.
90. What judgment does the Word of God pass upon thieves and robbers?

div.p: They shall not inherit the kingdom of God.

p.hi: 1 Cor. 6:10. Neither thieves nor extortioners shall inherit the kingdom of God.
91. May we not do with our property what we please?

div.p: No; we are but keepers of God's gifts, and we must once give an account of how we have used them.

p.hi: 92. What does God require of us in the seventh commandment?

div.p: We must be honest and unselfish in all our dealings, and help our neighbor to improve and protect his property and living.

p.hi: 1 John 3:17. [R. V.] But whoso hath the world's goods, and beholdeth his brother in need, and shutteth up his compassion from him, how doth the love of God abide in him?
James 2:13. For he shall have judgment without mercy that hath showed no mercy.

div.head: THE EIGHTH COMMANDMENT.

p.hi: Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbor.

div.p: That is,
We should fear and love God, and not tell lies about our neighbor, nor betray, slander, or defame him; but excuse him, speak well of him, and look upon all his acts as well-meant.

p.hi: 93. What is "false witness"?

div.p: All untruthful speaking about our neighbor, in or out of court.

p.hi: 94. How does one bear false witness in court?

div.p: When a witness swears to a lie, and when a judge decides wrong to be right, and right to be wrong.

p.hi: 95. How do we bear false witness out of court?

div.p: When we tell lies about our neighbor and slander or defame him in our conversation.

p.hi: Eph. 4:25. Wherefore, putting away lying, speak every man truth with his neighbor.
96. Do we sin when we speak truthfully of our neighbor's faults?

div.p: Yes; when we do so with an unloving heart, either because we wish to hurt our neighbor, or thoughtlessly and in gossiping.

p.hi: Matt. 12:36. Every idle word that man shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment.
97. What does God require of us in the eighth commandment?

div.p: We must always be truthful, excuse, and speak well of our neighbor, as far as truth permits, and look upon all his acts as well-meant.

p.hi: 1 Cor. 13:5–7. Love thinketh no evil; rejoiceth not in iniquity, but rejoiceth in the truth; beareth all things, believeth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things.

div.head: THE NINTH COMMANDMENT.

p.hi: Thou shalt not covet thy neighbor's house.

div.p: That is,
We should fear and love God, and not by deceit or craft seek to gain our neighbor's inheritance or home, nor try to get it though we seem to have some right thereto, but help him to keep his own.

div.head: THE TENTH COMMANDMENT.

p.hi: Thou shalt not covet thy neighbor's wife, nor his man-servant, nor his maid-servant, nor his cattle, nor anything that is his.

div.p: That is,
We should fear and love God, and not estrange, force, or entice away from our neighbor, his wife, servants, or cattle, but urge them to stay and do their duty.

p.hi: 98. What do the ninth and tenth commandments forbid?

div.p: All sinful desire to get what belongs to our neighbor.

p.hi: 99. What does God require of us in the ninth and tenth commandments?

div.p: We must heartily wish our neighbor all good, rejoice in his success, and help him to keep what he owns.

p.hi: 100. What, then, does God require of us in His holy Law?

div.p: Perfect purity and holiness in all our thoughts and desires, words and acts.

p.hi: James 2:10. Whosoever shall keep the whole law, and yet offend in one point, he is guilty of all.
Matt 5:48. Be ye therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.
101. What does God say of all his commandment?
I the Lord thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the
third and fourth generation of them that hate me; and showing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments.

div.p: That is,
God threatens to punish all who transgress these commandments; we should therefore fear His wrath, and do nothing against them.
On the other hand He promises grace and every blessing to all who keep these commandments; we should therefore love Him and trust in Him, and gladly do according to His commandments.

p.hi: 102. Of what does God remind us by these words?

div.p: He reminds us of the fact that He is a just God, who in His holy wrath punishes every sin.

p.hi: 103. What is sin?

div.p: Sin is any thought or feeling, word or act, which is contrary to God's holy Law.

p.hi: 104. What is meant by original sin?

div.p: Original sin is the inborn wickedness, deep corruption, and evil disposition, of the human heart.

p.hi: Ps. 51:5. Behold, I was shapen in iniquity; and in sin did my mother conceive me.
Rom. 5:12. By one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned.
105. What is actual sin?

div.p: Actual sin is all evil thoughts and desires, words and acts, springing from original sin.

p.hi: 106. Is neglecting to do good as sinful as doing wrong?

div.p: Yes, indeed; to him that knoweth to do good, and doeth it not, to him it is sin.
James 4:17.

p.hi: 107. Do the children of God always live according to the will of their heavenly Father?

div.p: They hate sin, and heartily strive to keep the law of God; but it is their experience that they sin every day, and that the new life within them is weak.

p.hi: Ps. 19:12. Who can understand his errors? cleanse thou me from secret faults?
Rom. 7:19. The good that I would I do not: but the evil which I would not, that I do.
108. How do the children of God feel and act when they find that they have sinned?

div.p: They are deeply grieved, they ask their heavenly Father to forgive them, and earnestly strive to put off sin.

p.hi: 109. What do the children of the world think of sin?

div.p: They love sin, and do not ask to be forgiven.

p.hi: 110. How does God threaten those who transgress His commandments?

div.p: He will visit, that is, punish, their wickedness.

p.hi: 111. How does God punish sin?

div.p: In soul and body; now and forever.

p.hi: Gal. 3:10. Cursed is every one that continueth not in all things which are written in the book of the law to do them.
112. What does God promise all who keep His commandments?

div.p: He will have mercy upon them in a thousand generations.

p.hi: 113. What is here understood by mercy?

div.p: Every blessing for soul and body, now and forever.

p.hi: 1 Tim. 4:8. Godliness is profitable unto all things, having promise of the life that now is, and of that which is to come.
114. What way of salvation does the Law then point out to us?

div.p: It says, Keep the commandments and you shall be saved.

p.hi: Luke 10:28. This do, and thou shalt live.

div.p: 115. Can any man, then, keep God's commandments so perfectly that he thereby is justified and saved?
No; every man is a sinner, and he lacks that perfect love which is the fulfillment of the law.

p.hi: Rom. 10:3. For they being ignorant of God's righteousness, and going about to establish their own righteousness, have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God.
116. But does the Word of God point out a way to us in which a sinner may be justified and saved?

div.p: Yes; in the blessed Gospel.

p.hi: Rom. 1:16. I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth.
117. What parts of the catechism treat about the gospel?

div.p: The four last parts.

div.head: THE THREE ARTICLES OF THE CREED.

p.hi: 118. Of what do the three articles treat?

div.p: Of the nature, will, and works of the triune God.

p.hi: 119. How do you know there is a God?

div.p: 1. From the world's creation, its preservation and government.

p.hi: Rom. 1:19, 20. That which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath showed it unto them.
For the invisible things of him since the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and divinity; so that they are without excuse.

div.p: 2. From my conscience, which is troubled when I do evil and rejoices when I do good.

p.hi: Rom. 2:15. They (the Gentiles) show the law written in their hearts, their conscience also bearing witness, and their thoughts the meanwhile accusing or else excusing one another.

div.p: 3. From the holy Scriptures wherein He still more clearly reveals Himself.

p.hi: John 1:18. No man hath seen God at any time; the only begotten Son, which is in the bosom of the Father, he hath declared him.
120. What is God?

div.p: God is a spirit, who is eternal and almighty; all-knowing and everywhere present; wise, good, and merciful; holy, true, and just.

p.hi: John 4:24. God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth.
Ps. 90:2. Before the mountains were brought forth, or even thou hadst formed the earth and the world, even from everlasting to everlasting thou art God.
Luke 1:37. With God nothing shall be impossible.
1 John 3:20. God knoweth all things.
Ps. 139:7. Whither shall I go from thy spirit! or thither shall I flee from thy presence?
Ps. 104:24. O Lord, how manifold are thy works! in wisdom hast thou made them all.
1 John 4:16. God is love.
Ps. 106:1. O give thanks unto the Lord; for he is good: for his mercy endureth forever.
Ps. 103:13. Like as a father pitieth his children, so the Lord pitieth them that fear him.
Isa. 6:3. Holy, holy, holy, is the Lord of hosts: all the earth is full of his glory.
Num. 23:19. God is not a man, that he should lie; neither the son of man, that he should repent; hath he said, and shall he not do it? Or hath he spoken, and shall he not make it good?
Rom. 2:6. God will render to every man according to his deeds.
121. Are there more Gods than one?

div.p: No; there is but one God, and there is none else besides Him.

p.hi: Deut. 6:4. Hear, O Israel: the Lord our God is one Lord.
122. How many persons are there in the Godhead?

div.p: Three; the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. These three are perfectly alike in character, and equal in greatness.

p.hi: Matt. 28:19. Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost.

div.head: CONCERNING CREATION.

p.hi: I believe in God the Father Almighty, Maker of heaven and earth.

div.p: That is,
I believe that God has made me and all other creatures; that He has given me body and soul, eyes, ears, and all other members, my reason, and all my senses.
I also believe that He preserves all He has made, and that He daily provides me with all I need; giving me clothing and food, home and family, and every good thing.
I further believe that He protects me from all danger, and keeps me from all evil; not because I have deserved it, but because He is a loving and merciful Father.
For all these blessings it is my duty to serve Him thankfully and obediently all the days of my life.
All this is certainly true.

p.hi: 123. What do you mean when you say, "I believe in God the Father"?

div.p: I believe that God is the Father of Jesus Christ, and my Father; and I surrender myself to Him, trusting with all my heart in His grace and love.

p.hi: 124. Why do we call God the Maker of heaven and earth?

div.p: Because He has made heaven and earth to come forth by His almighty Word.

p.hi: Ps. 33:9. He spoke, and it was done; he commanded, and it stood fast.
125. Does God yet care for what He has made?

div.p: Yes; by His watchful care He preserves and governs all things.

p.hi: 126. How does God preserve all things?

div.p: He lets all things continue as long as He thinks well, and He cares like a father for all His creatures.

p.hi: Gen. 8:22. While the earth remaineth, seedtime and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and winter, and day and night, shall not cease.
Acts 17:25. He giveth to all life, and breath, and all things.
Ps. 104:27. These wait all upon thee; that thou mayest give them their meat in due season.
127. For whom does God care most?

div.p: For man; and especially for His believing children.

p.hi: Matt. 6:26, 27, 28, 30. Behold the fowls of the air: for they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feedeth them. Are ye not much better than they?
Which of you by taking thought, can add one cubit to his stature?
And why take ye thought for raiment? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow; they toil not, neither do they spin.
Wherefore, if God so clothe the grass of the field, which to-day is, and to-morrow is cast into the oven, shall he not much more clothe you, O ye of little faith?
128. How does God govern men with regard to their sins?

div.p: He suffers them to sin, sets limits to their sinning, and so guides the result that everything will be for their good who love Him.

p.hi: Gen. 50:20. [R. V.] Ye meant evil against me; but God meant it for good.
129. Do we always understand the ways of God's providence?

div.p: No; His ways are often hidden from our eyes; but even then they are the kindest and best.

p.hi: Isa. 55:8, 9. For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, saith the Lord.
For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts.
130. In whose care may you therefore safely leave yourself?

div.p: In God's care, who protects me from all danger, and keeps me from all evil.

p.hi: 1 Pet. 5:7. Casting all your care upon him: for he careth for you.
131. Have you deserved all this?

div.p: Not in the least; He does all this, not because I have deserved it, but because He is a loving and merciful Father.

p.hi: Gen. 32:10. I am not worthy of the least of all the mercies, and of all the truth, which thou hast showed unto thy servant.
132. What do you owe God for all his goodness?

div.p: It is my duty to serve Him thankfully and obediently all the days of my life.

p.hi: Ps. 103:2. Bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits.
133. Which are the most excellent of the heavenly creatures?

div.p: The holy angels.

p.hi: 134. What is the work of the holy angels?

div.p: They praise God, and serve him, especially by ministering to His children.

p.hi: Heb. 1:14. Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation.
135. Are there not also evil angels?

div.p: Yes; there are evil angels who have fallen away from God through pride and disobedience, and are forever excluded from fellowship with Him. The devil is their king.

p.hi: 136. Which is the most excellent of the earthly creatures?

div.p: Man, to whom God gave power to rule over the earth.

p.hi: 137. What was the character of man as he was made by God?

div.p: Adam and Eve were innocent, without sin, and like God.

p.hi: Gen. 1:27. [R. V.] God made man in his own image, in the image of God made he him: male and female made he them.
138. In what did the image of God in man consist?

div.p: In true wisdom, righteousness and holiness, peace and joy.

p.hi: Eph. 4:24. Put on the new man, which after God is created in righteousness and holiness.
139. What benefit did the human body have from the image of God?

div.p: Perfect health, immortality, and a life free from care in Paradise.

p.hi: 140. Did our first parents remain innocent and without sin?

div.p: No; they sinned and lost the image of God, and thus sin and death entered into the world.

p.hi: Gen. 2:17. In the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die.
Rom. 6:23. The wages of sin is death.
141. In what did their sin consist?

div.p: It consisted especially in the unbelief of their hearts and in their selfishness and disobedience.

p.hi: 142. Who led them astray?

div.p: They permitted the devil to lead them astray.

p.hi: John 8:44. The devil was a murderer from the beginning, and abode not in the truth, because there is no truth in him. For he is a liar, and the father of it.
143. How has sin injured the human soul?

div.p: 1. It has darkened the understanding.

p.hi: See 1 Cor. 2:14.

div.p: 2. It has made the will incapable of what is good, and desirous of all that is evil.

p.hi: Rom. 8:7. The carnal mind is enmity against God.

div.p: 3. It has disturbed the peace and joy of conscience.

p.hi: 144. How has sin injured the human body?

div.p: Sin has made the body a tool of every evil passion, and has brought upon it disease, distress, countless pains, and finally death.

p.hi: Job 14:1, 2. Man that is born of a woman is of few days, and full of trouble.
He cometh forth like a flower, and is cut down: he fleeth also as a shadow, and continueth not.
145. Have all men become sinners through the fall of our first parents?

div.p: Yes; sin and death have spread from our first parents to the whole human race.

p.hi: Rom. 5:18. By the offence of one judgment came upon all men to condemnation.
146. Will God, then, leave all men to perish?

div.p: No; God has in love sent His Son Jesus Christ to save man.

p.hi: John 3:16. For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.
147. When was this Savior first promised to the world?

div.p: Immediately after the fall.

p.hi: Gen. 3:15. The seed of the woman shall bruise the serpent's head.
148. When was Christ sent to the world?

div.p: In the fulness of time; that is, the time appointed and prepared by God Himself.

p.hi: Gal. 4:4. [R. V.] When the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son born of a woman.

div.head: CONCERNING REDEMPTION.

p.hi: I believe in Jesus Christ His only Son, our Lord; who was conceived by the Holy Ghost, born of the Virgin Mary; suffered under Pontius Pilate, was crucified, dead, and buried; He descended into hell; the third day He rose again from the dead; He ascended into heaven, and sitteth on the right hand of God the Father Almighty; from whence He shall come to judge the quick and the dead.

div.p: That is,

I believe that Jesus Christ is true God, begotten of the Father from eternity; I also believe that He is true man, born of the Virgin Mary; that He is my Lord, who has redeemed me, a lost and condemned sinner; who has freed me from sin, from death, and from the power of Satan, not with gold or silver, but with His holy and precious blood and His innocent death.

All this He has done that I might be His own, and that I might serve Him in righteousness, innocence, and happiness, and live and reign with Him in His kingdom forever, even as He arose from the dead, lives and reigns through all eternity.
All this is certainly true.

p.hi: 149. What do you mean when you say "I believe in Jesus Christ?"

div.p: Trusting in Jesus Christ with all my heart, I surrender myself to Him as my only Savior from sin, and death, and the power of Satan.

p.hi: Acts 4:12. Neither is there salvation in any other: for there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved.
150. Who is Jesus Christ?

div.p: The Son of God and the Son of Mary, true God and true man.

p.hi: 151. How does Christ have divine nature?

div.p: He is begotten of the Father from eternity.

p.hi: 152. How does Christ have human nature?

div.p: He is conceived by the Holy Ghost, and born of the Virgin Mary.

p.hi: 153. What does the Bible say about Christ being true God?

div.p: The Bible calls Him the only begotten Son of God, and one with the Father.
The Bible also expressly calls Him God.

p.hi: John 10:30. I and my Father are one.
John 5:23. All men should honor the Son, even as they honor the Father. He that honoreth not the Son honoreth not the Father which hath sent Him.
1 John 5:20. This is the true God, and eternal life.
John 1:1. In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
John 3:16.
154. What does the Bible say about Christ being both God and man?

div.p: It says, The Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us. John 1:14.
And,
When the fulness of the time came, God sent forth His Son, born of a woman. [R. V.] Gal. 4:4.

p.hi: 155. Why must the Son of God become true man?

div.p: In order that He might suffer and die for us.

p.hi: 156. Why must our Savior be true God?

div.p: In order that His death and His blood might have everlasting power to atone for sin.

p.hi: 157. Is Jesus conceived and born with sin?

div.p: No; He is conceived by the Holy Ghost and therefore without sin.

p.hi: Luke 1:35. The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God.
158. What does the name Jesus signify?

div.p: A Savior.

p.hi: Matt. 1:21. Thou shalt call His name Jesus: for He shall save His people from their sins.
159. What does the name Christ signify?

div.p: The same as Messiah; that is, the Anointed or the Consecrated.

p.hi: 160. How was Jesus anointed?

div.p: He was anointed with the Holy Ghost and with power. Acts 10:38.

p.hi: 161. For what offices was Jesus anointed and consecrated?

div.p: The offices of High Priest, Prophet, and King.

p.hi: 162. What is Christ's work as High Priest?

div.p: He offered up Himself a sacrifice for our sins, and ever prays for us.

p.hi: Heb. 7:26, 27. [R. V.] For such a high priest became us,—who needeth not daily as those high priests, to offer up sacrifices, first for his own sins, and then for the sins of the people: for this He did once for all, when he offered up himself.
Rom. 8:34. Jesus Christ, who also maketh intercession for us.
163. What is Christ's work as Prophet?

div.p: He teaches us the will of God concerning our salvation.

p.hi: Luke 24: 19. Jesus of Nazareth, which was a prophet mighty in deed and word before God and all the people.
164. What is Christ's work as King?

div.p: He governs and keeps His children, and defends them against their enemies.

p.hi: Luke 1:33. And he shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever; and of his kingdom there shall be no end.
Rev. 17:14. He is the Lord of lords, and the King of kings.
165. How are the believers named after Christ?

div.p: They are called Christians; meaning, "the anointed".

p.hi: 1 John 2:20. Ye have an anointing from the Holy One, and ye know all things.
166. With what means has Christ redeemed us?

div.p: He has paid for our sins with His holy and precious blood and His innocent death, and He has fulfilled the law in our stead with His holy life and His perfect obedience.

p.hi: 1 Pet. 1:18, 19. [R. V.] Ye know that ye were not redeemed with corruptible things, as silver and gold, from your vain manner of life; but with precious blood, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot, even the blood of Christ.
167. Whom has Christ redeemed?

div.p: He has redeemed me, a lost and condemned sinner.

p.hi: 168. Has not Christ redeemed all mankind?

div.p: Yes, He has; He gave Himself a ransom for all. 1 Tim. 2:6.

p.hi: 1 John 2:2. He is the propitiation for our sins; and not for ours only, but also for the sins of the whole world.
169. But are not many, thus redeemed, yet lost?

div.p: Yes, indeed; many reject Him because of their unbelief and love of sin.

p.hi: 2 Pet. 2:1. Denying the Lord who bought them.
John 3:18. He that believeth not is condemned already, because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God.
170. Who get a share in the redemption of Christ?

div.p: Those who repent their sins and believe in Him.

p.hi: 171. What benefit does the believer have from the redemption of Christ?

div.p: By this redemption he is freed from sin, from death, and from the power of Satan.

p.hi: 172. In what way is the believer freed from sin by the redemption of Christ?

div.p: 1. The guilt and punishment of sin are removed from him.

p.hi: Col. 1:14. We have redemption through His blood, even the forgiveness of sins.

div.p: 2. Sin rules over him no longer.

p.hi: Rom. 6:14. Sin shall not have dominion over you.

div.p: 3. When he dies, sin is entirely rooted out from him.

p.hi: 173. In what way is the believer freed from death by the redemption of Christ?

div.p: Spiritual death has lost its power over him, temporal death is but an entrance into perfect life, and eternal death he no longer fears.

p.hi: John 11:25, 26. Jesus said unto her, I am the resurrection and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live; and whosoever liveth and believeth in me shall never die.
174. In what way is the believer freed from the power of Satan by the redemption of Christ?

div.p: Satan has no power over the believer, unless the believer yield himself into his service.

p.hi: Heb. 2:14. [R. V.] Since then the children are sharers in flesh and blood, he also himself in like manner partook of the same; that through death he might bring to nought him that had the power of death, that is, the devil.
175. For what purpose has Christ redeemed you?

div.p: He has redeemed me in order that I might be His own, live with Him in His kingdom, and serve Him in righteousness, innocence, and happiness.

p.hi: 1 Cor. 6:20. [R. V.] Ye are not your own, for ye were bought with a price; glorify God therefore in your body.
Titus 2:14. [R. V.] He gave himself for us, that he might redeem us from all iniquity, and purify unto himself a people for his own possession, zealous of good works.
176. What did Christ do in order to become our Savior and Redeemer?

div.p: He humbled Himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross. Phil. 2:8.

p.hi: 177. How many steps do you notice in the humiliation of Christ?

div.p: Five: the birth in poverty; the suffering; the crucifixion; the death; the burial.

p.hi: 178. Why did Christ begin His life on earth with the birth in poverty?

div.p: He began His life in poverty to show that His kingdom is not of this world, and that we might be made rich through His poverty.

p.hi: 179. When was the suffering of Christ greatest?

div.p: In the night before His death, and on Good Friday, when He was delivered into the hands of His enemies, and was bound, beaten, scourged, crowned with thorns, and finally nailed to the cross.

p.hi: 180. Did Christ suffer bodily pain only?

div.p: No; His greatest suffering was a fearful anguish of soul on account of our sins.

p.hi: 181. When in particular did he suffer this anguish?

div.p: In the garden, when His sweat was as drops of blood and He said, "My soul is exceeding sorrowful unto death"; and on the cross, when He cried, "My God, my God, why hast Thou forsaken me?"

p.hi: Isa. 53:4, 5. Surely he hath borne our griefs, and carried our sorrows:
But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed.
182. How did Christ act through all this suffering?

div.p: He was patient as a lamb that is lead to the slaughter. Isa. 53:7.

p.hi: 183. What did Christ accomplish for us by His death on the cross?

div.p: By His death He has paid the wages of sin, which is death.

p.hi: Rom. 5:10. When we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son.
184. What comfort do we have from the burial of Christ?

div.p: He has buried our sins, hallowed our graves, and taken away their horror.

p.hi: 185. How should we look upon the life and suffering of Christ in His humiliation?

div.p: We should look upon His life and His suffering as an atonement for our sins, and as an example to the believer of holiness in life and patience in suffering.

p.hi: 1 Pet. 2:21. Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow His steps.
186. Did Christ remain in humiliation and death?

div.p: No; God exalted Him and gave Him a name which is above every name. Phil. 2:9.

p.hi: 187. How many steps do you notice in the exaltation of Christ?

div.p: Five: His descent into hell; His resurrection; His ascension; His session at the right hand of the Father; His coming to judge the quick and the dead.

p.hi: 188. What did Christ accomplish when he descended into hell?

div.p: He made known the victory which He had won over the devil, and preached to the spirits in prison. 1 Pet. 3:18, 19.

p.hi: 189. What benefit do we have from the resurrection of Christ?

div.p: 1. The resurrection assures us that Christ is the Son of God, and that He has conquered death and fully satisfied for our sins.

p.hi: Rom. 1:4. Declared to be the Son of God by the resurrection from the dead.
1 Cor. 15:14. If Christ be not risen, then is our preaching vain, and your faith is also vain.

div.p: 2. The resurrection gives us power to arise from spiritual death, and to live a new and holy life.

p.hi: Rom. 6:4. As Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, even so we also should walk in newness of life.

div.p: 3. The resurrection assures us that our bodies shall arise in glory on the last day.

p.hi: 190. What command did Christ give His disciples before His ascension?

div.p: He commanded them to go out into the whole world and preach the gospel to all nations. [Missions.]

p.hi: 191. What is meant by the ascension of Christ?

div.p: He left the earth, so that He is no longer visibly present, and He entered into His Father's glory to prepare a place for us in the heavenly mansions.

p.hi: John 14:2. In my Father's house are many mansions; I go to prepare a place for you.
192. What does the ascension of Christ teach us?

div.p: It teaches us to be heavenly-minded, and to have a desire to depart and be with Christ.

p.hi: Col. 3:1. If ye then be risen with Christ, seek those things which are above, where Christ sitteth on the right hand of God.
193. What does Christ's session on the right hand of the Father signify?

div.p: It signifies that He shares also as true man in the power and glory of God, and rules over all things.

p.hi: 1 Pet. 3:22. [R. V.] He is on the right hand of God, having gone into heaven; angels and authorities and powers being made subject to Him.
194. What benefit do we have from Christ's session on the right hand of the Father?

div.p: He protects His kingdom from its enemies, prays for us, and sends us His Holy Spirit.

p.hi: 195. Is Christ no longer present on earth?

div.p: Yes; He is present in a real, though invisible, manner.

p.hi: Matt. 28:20. And lo, I am with you always, even unto the end of the world.
196. When will He again come to earth in a visible manner?

div.p: On the last day, when He comes to judge the quick and the dead.

p.hi: Luke 21:27. And then shall they see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.
2 Cor. 5:10. We must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ; that every one may receive the things done in the body, according to that he hath done, whether it be good or bad.
197. By what rule will Christ judge us?

div.p: He will judge us by His Word.

p.hi: John 12:48. The Word that I have spoken, the same shall judge him in the last day.
198. Is it sufficient that you know all these things about Christ and hold them to be true?

div.p: No; the Holy Spirit must teach me to know Christ in a true and living faith.

div.head: CONCERNING SANCTIFICATION.

p.hi: I believe in the Holy Ghost; the holy Christian church, the communion of saints; the forgiveness of sins; the resurrection of the body; and life everlasting. Amen.

div.p: That is,

I believe that I cannot through my own strength believe in Jesus Christ my Lord, or come to Him. This is the work of the Holy Spirit alone, who has called me through the gospel, enlightened me with His gifts, and sanctified and preserved me in the true faith;
Even as He calls, gathers, enlightens, and sanctifies the whole Christian church on earth, and preserves it in fellowship with Jesus Christ in the one true faith.
In this Christian church He daily forgives me and all believers all our sins, and He will raise up me and all the dead on the last day, and will give me and all believers everlasting life.
All this is certainly true.

p.hi: 199. What do you mean when you say, "I believe in the Holy Ghost"?

div.p: I trust with all my heart in the Holy Ghost as my guide and my sanctifier, who gives me strength to believe in Jesus and to live according to His will.

p.hi: 1 Cor. 12:3. No man can say that Jesus is the Lord, but by the Holy Ghost.
200. Who is the Holy Ghost?

div.p: The Holy Ghost is true God together with the Father and the Son.

p.hi: 1 Cor. 2:10. The Spirit searcheth all things, yea, the deep things of God.
1 Cor. 3:16. Know ye not that ye are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you.
201. What is the work of the Holy Spirit?

div.p: To call, enlighten, sanctify, and preserve.

p.hi: 202. How does the Holy Spirit call us?

div.p: The Holy Spirit calls us by awakening in our hearts a deep sense of sin, and by inviting us to accept the grace of God in Christ.

p.hi: Eph. 5:14. Awake thou that sleepest, and arise from the dead, and Christ shall give thee light.
203. By what means does the Holy Spirit call us?

div.p: By the Word of God; using the law to awaken our hearts, and the gospel to invite us to Christ.

p.hi: Rom. 3:20. By the law is the knowledge of sin.
2 Thess. 2:14. He called you by our gospel, to the obtaining of the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ.
204. What means does God use to make us heed the call of the Holy Spirit?

div.p: To this end He often uses suffering, often blessings, often the example of others, and such other means as may lead us to reflect.

p.hi: 205. Do all obey the call of the Holy Spirit?

div.p: No; many resist the Holy Spirit, and will not repent and come to Christ.

p.hi: Acts 7:51. Ye do always resist the Holy Ghost.
Isa. 65:2. I have spread out my hands all the day to a rebellious people.
206. When does a person harden his heart?

div.p: A person hardens his heart when he persistently despises and opposes the voice of the Holy Spirit in his conscience.

p.hi: 207. Who obey the call of the Holy Spirit?

div.p: They who repent their sins and believe the Gospel.

p.hi: Mark. 1:15. The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand: repent ye, and believe the gospel.
208. What is it to repent?

div.p: He who truly repents, feels his sins with shame and sorrow, he freely confesses his sins to God, and earnestly seeks the grace of God in Christ.

p.hi: Isa. 55:7. Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts: and let him return unto the Lord, and He will have mercy upon him; and to our God, for He will abundantly pardon.
2 Cor. 7:10. [R. V.] Godly sorrow worketh repentance unto salvation, a repentance which bringeth no regret: but the sorrow of the world worketh death.
Ps. 32:5. I acknowledged my sin unto thee; and thou forgavest the iniquity of my sin.
209. How do we learn that the grace of God is found in Christ?

div.p: We learn this through the enlightenment of the Holy Spirit.

p.hi: 210. What is meant by the enlightenment of the Holy Spirit?

div.p: Through the enlightenment of the Holy Spirit our knowledge of the Gospel truths becomes a living and saving knowledge to our hearts.

p.hi: John 14:26. But the Comforter, the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you.
John 16:13. When he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth.
211. Of what nature is our knowledge of these truths before the Holy Spirit has enlightened our hearts?

div.p: It is a dead knowledge only, which does not lead to repentance and faith, but leaves us in our sins.

p.hi: 212. What is the true and living faith in Jesus Christ?

div.p: This is faith, that a repentant sinner lays hold of Christ as his only Savior from sin, and death, and the power of Satan;
That he takes refuge with Christ and His righteousness, and builds thereon with the confidence of his whole heart.

p.hi: 213. Can only a repentant sinner have this faith in Christ?

div.p: Yes; the faith which lays hold of Christ and His righteousness, can be wrought in that heart only which bitterly feels the pain and misery of living in sin.

p.hi: Matt. 9:12. They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick.
214. Is the true and living faith always and in all persons equally strong?

div.p: No; it is often very weak and scarcely able to avail itself of the grace of God.

p.hi: Mark 9:24. Lord, I believe; help thou my unbelief.
215. Whereby may we know whether this weak faith is true and living?

div.p: The true and living faith is known by an earnest hatred of sin, and an eager longing for grace.

p.hi: 216. Does God accept this weak faith?

div.p: Yes, indeed; only it be true and sincere.

p.hi: Isa. 42:3. A bruised reed shall he not break, and the smoking flax shall he not quench.
217. What benefit do we have from the true and living faith in Jesus Christ?

div.p: By faith we are justified, born anew, sanctified, and finally saved forever.

p.hi: 218. What is Justification?

div.p: Justification is the gracious act of God whereby He for Christ's sake acquits a repentant and believing sinner of his sin and guilt, and looks upon him, in Christ, as though he had never sinned.

p.hi: 2 Cor. 5:21. For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin that we might be made the righteousness of God in him.
Rom. 3:24. (They are) justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus.
219. What, then, does the believer receive through justification?

div.p: He receives the forgiveness of sins, and is adopted as a child of God.

p.hi: Eph. 1:7. In whom we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of sins, according to the riches of his grace.
Gal. 3:26. For ye are the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus.
Acts 10:43. To him give all the prophets witness, that through his name whosoever believeth in him shall receive remission of sins.
220. What moves God to forgive sin so freely?

div.p: His everlasting love and mercy alone.

p.hi: 221. For whose sake does God forgive us our sins?

div.p: For Christ's sake, who has satisfied for the sins of the whole world by His death on the cross.

p.hi: John 1:29. Behold the lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.
222. To what does the forgiveness of sins necessarily lead?

div.p: The forgiveness of sins leads to the full enjoyment of the blessed rights which belong to a child of God; it also gives free access to the Father's fellowship and blessing, and to the glorious inheritance of eternal life.

p.hi: Ps. 32:1, 2. Blessed is he whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is covered.
Blessed is the man unto whom the Lord imputeth not iniquity, and in whose spirit there is no guile.
Rom. 8:17. And if [we are] children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ.
223. What is the New Birth?

div.p: The New Birth is the gracious work of the Holy Spirit whereby He, through His indwelling in our hearts, renews the image of God in us, and thus creates a new spiritual man.

p.hi: 2 Cor. 5:17. If any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things have passed away; behold, all things are new.
John 1:12, 13. But as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his name:
Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God.
224. What change is wrought in us in the New Birth?

div.p: We get a new heart or a new spiritual life; namely,

lg.l: In the understanding, a new spiritual light;
In the conscience, real peace and joy;
In the will, a holy desire and a steadfast purpose.

p.hi: Ezek. 36:26. A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you a heart of flesh.
Eph. 4:24. Put on the new man, which after God is created in righteousness and true holiness.
Gal. 5:22. The fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace.
225. In what does this new life really consist?

div.p: In consists in love to God who first loved us.

p.hi: 226. By what means is the New Birth accomplished?

div.p: In little children it is accomplished by water and the Spirit in baptism; but in those who have fallen from the grace of their baptism, also by the Word of God.

p.hi: John 3:5. Jesus answered, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God.
1 Peter 1:23. Being born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, by the word of God, which liveth and abideth forever.
227. Is the New Birth necessary to our salvation?

div.p: Yes, indeed; except a man be born anew, he cannot see the kingdom of God. John 3: 3. [R. V.]

p.hi: John 3:6. That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit, is spirit.
228. What does the Holy Spirit further work in the believer?

div.p: He sanctifies and preserves him.

p.hi: 229. What is Sanctification?

div.p: Sanctification is the gracious work of the Holy Spirit whereby He day by day renews the believer more and more after the image of God.

p.hi: 230. How is the daily renewal accomplished?

div.p: The old man, or sin, is put away more and more, and the new man, or the new spiritual life, appears more and more in all our conduct.

p.hi: Eph. 4:22–24. [R. V.] Put away, as concerning your former manner of life, the old man, which waxeth corrupt after the lusts of deceit;
And be ye renewed in the spirit of your mind,
And put on the new man, which after God hath been created in righteousness and holiness of truth.
231. How does this new conduct appear in the daily life of a Christian?

div.p: A Christian denies himself, strives against the devil, the world, and his own flesh; he grows in love toward God and man, and seeks to do the will of God in all things.

p.hi: Matt. 16:24. If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.
1 Cor. 16:13. Watch ye, stand fast in the faith, quit you like men, be strong.
1 Tim. 6:12. Fight the good fight of faith, lay hold on eternal life, whereunto thou art also called, and hast professed a good profession before many witnesses.
232. Is the believer, then, justified and saved by his own good works?

div.p: No; our best works avail nothing to this end: we must build our hope of salvation on Christ alone and His righteousness.

p.hi: Luk. 17:10. When ye shall have done all these things which are commanded you, say, We are unprofitable servants: we have done that which was our duty to do.
233. What is the work of Preservation done by the Holy Spirit?

div.p: Preservation is the gracious work of the Holy Spirit whereby He keeps us, through all temptations, in the true and living faith in Jesus, until the end.

p.hi: Phil. 1:6. [R. V.] He which began a good work in you will perfect it until the day of Jesus Christ.
