234. By what means does the Holy Spirit sanctify and preserve the believer?

div.p: By the Word of God and the Lord's Supper.

p.hi: 235. How does the Holy Spirit preserve the believer?

div.p: He teaches and guides, corrects and comforts him.

p.hi: 236. What are they called whom the Holy Spirit thus sanctifies and preserves in faith?

div.p: They are called the children of God; the Elect of God; Holy and Beloved; Members of the Body of Christ. In a body they make up the holy Christian church.

p.hi: 237. What is the holy Christian church?

div.p: The holy Christian Church is the congregation of saints or true believers, where the Word of God is preached and the sacraments are administered according to the ordinance of God.

p.hi: 238. Why is the church called holy?

div.p: The church is called holy because of the indwelling of the Holy Spirit, who performs His sanctifying work in all its members. For this reason the church is called holy, in spite of its sins and shortcomings.

p.hi: 1 Peter 2:9. Ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should show forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light.
239. Why is the church called universal?

div.p: The church is called universal because its object is to gather all nations, and because it includes all true believers of all times and all places.

p.hi: 240. What is the state of the church on earth?

div.p: The church of God on earth is militant.

p.hi: 241. Who are the enemies of the church?

div.p: The enemies of the church are the devil, the world, and our own flesh. Its last enemy is death.

p.hi: 242. What will be the state of the church in heaven?

div.p: It will be triumphant, because all its enemies are conquered.

p.hi: Rev. 7:9, 10. After this I beheld, and, lo, a great multitude, which no man could number, of all nations, and kindreds, and people, and tongues, stood before the throne, and before the Lamb, clothed with white robes, and palms in their hands;
And cried with a loud voice, saying, Salvation to our God which sitteth upon the throne, and unto the Lamb.
243. Is the holy Christian church found in this place?

div.p: Yes; in the congregation, which in the Scriptures is called "the body of Jesus Christ", and "the house of God."

p.hi: 244. Are all the members of the organized body, called a congregation, true Christians?

div.p: No; in this organized body both hypocrites and true Christians are found.

p.hi: 245. Who are hypocrites?

div.p: Hypocrites are they who indeed make outward confession of Christ, but who inwardly and in their conduct deny Him.

p.hi: 2 Tim. 3:5. Having a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof.
246. Should not the congregation remove these hypocrites from its midst?

div.p: Yes; the congregation should expel the openly ungodly and unbelieving; but it cannot judge concerning the secret thoughts of the heart.

p.hi: 1 Cor. 5:13. Therefore put away from among yourselves that wicked person.
247. Who, then, are true Christians and the real members of the congregation?

div.p: They who believe in Christ with all their heart, and confess Him both in word and deed.

p.hi: Rom. 10:10. For with the heart man believeth unto righteousness: and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation.
248. What is the intimate fellowship called in which all true Christians live with one another?

div.p: The Communion of Saints.

p.hi: Eph. 4:4–6. There is one body, and one Spirit, even as ye are called in one hope of your calling;
One Lord, one faith, one baptism,
One God and Father of all, who is above all, and through all, and in you all.
249. What precious gift does the Holy Spirit bestow upon us in this Christian church?

div.p: In this Christian church He daily forgives me and all believers all our sins.

p.hi: 250. But does a sanctified person need the forgiveness of sins every day?

div.p: Yes; because sanctification is never perfected in this life, and sin cleaves to a Christian as long as he is in the world.

p.hi: 251. Whom has God given power to declare the forgiveness of sins?

div.p: The congregation, through its ministers. [Absolution.]

p.hi: Matt. 18:18. Verily I say unto you, Whatsoever ye shall bind on earth shall be bound in heaven: and whatsoever ye shall loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven.
252. What is required that a Christian may receive the forgiveness of sins every day?

div.p: That he repents every day, or that he daily feels his sins with deep shame and sorrow, confesses his sins to God, and earnestly seeks the grace of God in Christ.

p.hi: 253. To whom should a repentant Christian confess his sins?

div.p: First of all to God; then, if he feels the need of it, to his pastor; finally to his neighbor, if he feels that he has wronged him in any way.

p.hi: Jas. 5:16. Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed.
1 John 1:9. If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
254. What does the daily forgiveness of sins work in the Christian?

div.p: The daily renewal, or that he day by day becomes more and more thankful to God, and increases in child-like obedience and faithfulness.

p.hi: 255. What becomes of the soul of the believer when he dies?

div.p: His soul goes home to God, where it rests from all strife and sorrow, in blessed fellowship with Him, until the resurrection of the body.

p.hi: Luke 23:43. Verily I say unto thee, To-day shalt thou be with me in paradise.
Rev. 14:13. Blessed are the dead which die in the Lord.
256. What is the resurrection of the body?

div.p: On the last day, when the Lord Jesus returns to earth, the bodies of the dead shall be made alive and shall be reunited with their souls.

p.hi: John 5:28, 29. The hour is coming, in which all that are in the graves shall hear his voice, and shall come forth; they that have done good, unto the resurrection of life; and they that have done evil, unto the resurrection of judgment.
257. What change shall then take place in the bodies of the believers?

div.p: Their bodies shall arise glorified and incorruptible, like unto the body of the risen Lord Jesus Christ.

p.hi: 1 Cor. 15:42, 43. It is sown in corruption; it is raised in incorruption:
It is sown in dishonor; it is raised in glory: it is sown in weakness; it is raised in power.
258. Where do all the risen go after the day of judgment?

div.p: The chosen enter into life everlasting; the condemned, into eternal death.

p.hi: Matt. 25:46. These shall go away into everlasting punishment; but the righteous into eternal life.
259. What is life everlasting?

div.p: Life everlasting is the blessed state in which the chosen are free from all evil, and live forever in fellowship with their God and Savior, praising God in the company of the holy angels, in everlasting peace and joy.

p.hi: Matt. 25:34. Then shall the King say unto them on his right hand, Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.
260. What is eternal death?

div.p: Eternal death is a dreadful state of separation from God, and everlasting anguish and suffering in hell.

p.hi: Matt. 25:41. Then shall he also say unto them on the left hand, Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels.
261. Who are thus condemned?

div.p: All who continue in impenitence and unbelief until death.

p.hi: John 3:36. He that believeth on the Son hath everlasting life: and he that believeth not the Son shall not see life; but the wrath of God abideth on him.
262. Who, on the other hand, obtain life everlasting?

div.p: All who continue steadfast in faith until death.

p.hi: Rev. 2:10. [R. V.] Be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee the crown of life.
263. Why do you end your confession of faith with the word Amen?

div.p: Because I know that what I here confess is certainly true.

p.hi: 264. What must you do that you may continue steadfast in faith and also increase therein?

div.p: I will pray God every day graciously to help and strengthen me.

div.head: THE LORD'S PRAYER.

p.hi: 265. What is prayer?

div.p: Prayer is the child-like communion of our hearts with God, in which we tell Him all our needs, and earnestly seek some gift from Him.

p.hi: 266. Who should pray?

div.p: All should pray; even little children.

p.hi: 267. But can all pray in this manner?

div.p: No, not the impenitent; their hearts are not right with God, and they do not seek Him earnestly.

p.hi: 268. In whose name must we pray?

div.p: We must pray in the name of Jesus.

p.hi: John 16:23. Verily, verily, I say unto you, Whatsoever ye shall ask the Father in my name, he will give it you.
269. What is meant by praying in the name of Jesus?

div.p: To pray in the name of Jesus is to ask on the strength of what He has done for us, and His intercession with the Father.

p.hi: 270. How should we pray?

div.p: We should pray humbly, confidently as a child, and reverently.

p.hi: 271. When should we pray?

div.p: The attitude of our hearts should be one of constant prayer, and our communion with God should not be confined to certain times and places, but we should speak with Him whenever we feel the need of it.

p.hi: 1 Thess. 5:17. Pray without ceasing.
Eph. 6: 18. Praying always with all prayer and supplication in the Spirit.
272. For whom should we pray?

div.p: We should pray not only for ourselves, but also for others,—even our enemies.

p.hi: 273. For what should we pray?

div.p: First of all we should pray for the spiritual gifts necessary to our salvation; but we may also pray for other gifts, both spiritual and temporal.

p.hi: Matt. 6:33. Seek ye first the kingdom of God and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.
1 Cor. 12:31. Covet earnestly the best gifts.
274. What must we always remember when we pray for things not necessary to our salvation?

div.p: We must always remember that God alone knows whether such a prayer answered would truly benefit us.
When asking such gifts we should always add, "Lord, if Thou wilt".

p.hi: Matt. 26:39. Not as I will, but as thou wilt.
275. Who teaches us to pray well?

div.p: The Holy Spirit, who is also called the Spirit of prayer.

p.hi: Rom. 8:26. We know not what we should pray for as we ought: but the Spirit itself maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered.
276. Which is the most perfect prayer?

div.p: The most perfect prayer is the Lord's Prayer, which Christ taught His own disciples.

p.hi: 277. Repeat this prayer.

div.p: Our Father, who art in heaven; hallowed be Thy name; Thy kingdom come; Thy will be done on earth, as it is in heaven; give us this day our daily bread; and forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us; and lead us not into temptation; but deliver us from evil; for Thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever and ever. Amen.

p.hi: 278. Why would God have us speak to Him as "Our Father"?

div.p: God would hereby tenderly invite us to believe that He is truly our Father, and we are truly His children, so that we may ask of Him with all cheerfulness and confidence, as dear children ask of their dear father.

p.hi: 279. Who alone can confidently call God Father?

div.p: God's children alone can call God their Father.

p.hi: 280. Why would God have us say "our Father" and not only "my Father"?

div.p: Because He would have us pray with one another and for one another, in spiritual fellowship.

p.hi: 281. What is the importance of the words "who art in heaven"?

div.p: By these words we are reminded of the exalted love and power of our heavenly Father, far above that of any earthly father.

p.hi: Matt. 7:11. If ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children, how much more shall your Father which is in heaven give good things to them that ask him?

div.head: THE FIRST PETITION.

p.hi: Hallowed be Thy name.

div.p: That is,
The name of God is indeed holy in itself; but we pray in this petition that it may be hallowed also among us.
This is done when the Word of God is rightly taught, and when we as the children of God live holy lives in obedience to the Word. This grant us, heavenly Father!
But he that teaches and lives otherwise than the Word of God teaches, profanes the name of God among us. From this preserve us, heavenly Father!

p.hi: 282. What do you pray for in the first petition?

div.p: I pray that the name of God may be hallowed among us.

p.hi: Ps. 72:19. Blessed be his glorious name forever: and let the whole earth be filled with his glory.
283. When is the name of God hallowed among us?

div.p: When the Word of God is rightly taught and is received into our hearts.

p.hi: 284. When do we hallow the name of God among our fellow men?

div.p: We hallow the name of God when we freely confess it before men in accordance with the Word, and when we as God's children live holy lives in obedience to the Word.

p.hi: Matt. 5:16. Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.
Matt. 10:32. Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven.
285. Who profanes the name of God?

div.p: He that teaches and lives otherwise than the Word of God teaches, profanes the name of God.

p.hi: Rom. 2:24. [R. V.] The name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you.

div.head: THE SECOND PETITION.

p.hi: Thy kingdom come.

div.p: That is,
The kingdom of God comes indeed of itself, without our prayer, but we pray in this petition that it may come also to us.
This is done when our heavenly Father gives us His Holy Spirit, so that by His grace we believe the Word of God, and live holy and Christ-like lives here in time, and in heaven forever.

p.hi: 286. What do you pray for in the second petition?

div.p: I pray that the kingdom of God may come.

p.hi: 287. What is meant, in a particular sense, by the kingdom of God which you pray for in this petition?

div.p: 1. The kingdom of grace, in which Christ makes every believer a partaker of righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit; and
2. The kingdom of glory in heaven, where the chosen live with Christ in perfect happiness.

p.hi: 288. What is meant by saying that the kingdom of God comes to us?

div.p: It means that we become partakers in it.

p.hi: 289. When does the kingdom of God come to us?

div.p: The kingdom of God comes to us when our heavenly Father gives us His Holy Spirit, so that by His grace we believe the Word of God.

p.hi: 290. What does the Holy Spirit work in them who thus by faith have become partakers in the kingdom of God?

div.p: They live holy and Christ-like lives here in time, and in heaven forever.

div.head: THE THIRD PETITION.

p.hi: Thy will be done on earth, as it is in heaven.

div.p: That is,
The good and gracious will of God is done indeed without our prayer; but we pray in this petition that it may be done also among us.
This is done when God brings to nothing all evil plans and purposes of the devil, the world, and our own flesh, that would hinder the hallowing of His name and the coming of His kingdom.
On the other hand, it is the good and gracious will of God to strengthen us and keep us steadfast in His Word and in faith, until death.

p.hi: 291. What do you pray for in the third petition?

div.p: I pray that the will of God may be done among us on earth, as it is in heaven.

p.hi: 292. What is the will of God?

div.p: It is the will of God that all His rational creatures should praise Him forever in perfect holiness and happiness.

p.hi: 293. Where is the will of God done in this manner?

div.p: In heaven, where the holy angels praise God in undisturbed peace and joy.

p.hi: Ps. 103:20, 21. Bless the Lord, ye his angels, that excel in strength, that do his commandments, hearkening unto the voice of his word.
Bless ye the Lord, all ye his hosts; ye ministers of his, that do his pleasure.
294. When is the will of God done among us, as it is in heaven?

div.p: When God brings to nothing all evil plans and purposes that would hinder the hallowing of His name and the coming of His kingdom, and when God strengthens us and keeps us steadfast in His Word and in faith, until death.

p.hi: 295. Who seek to prevent the will of God from being done among us?

div.p: The devil, the world, and our own flesh.

p.hi: 296. Who, on the other hand, will help us to do the will of God?

div.p: God, who is merciful and faithful, will Himself help us to do His will.

p.hi: 1 Thess. 5:24. Faithful is he that calleth you, who also will do it.

div.head: THE FOURTH PETITION.

p.hi: Give us this day our daily bread.

div.p: That is,

God gives daily bread indeed without our prayer even to the wicked; but we pray in this petition that He would help us to appreciate His benefits, that we may receive our daily bread with thanksgiving.

By daily bread is meant all those things which are needed for our support and well-being in life, as food and clothing, home and property, happy family relations, a good government, favorable weather, peace and health, faithful friends, good neighbors, and the like.

p.hi: 297. What do you pray for in the fourth petition?

div.p: I pray God to give me daily bread.

p.hi: 298. What is meant by daily bread?

div.p: By daily bread is meant all those things which are needed for our support and well-being in life, as food and clothing, home and property, etc.

p.hi: 299. Of what does the word "daily" remind you?

div.p: I must be content with that which God gives me.

p.hi: Prov. 30:8. Give me neither poverty nor riches: feed me with food convenient for me.
1 Tim. 6:6. Godliness with contentment is great gain.
300. Why are the words "this day" added?

div.p: They are added that I should not be anxious for the morrow, but let each day bear its own burdens.

p.hi: Matt. 6:34.
301. Does God give daily bread to those only who pray for it?

div.p: No; He gives daily bread also to the wicked, but they receive it without thanksgiving, and miss His blessing.

p.hi: Matt. 5:45. He maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust.
302. How should the children of God receive their daily bread?

div.p: They should ask God to bless their daily bread, and return Him thanks for it.

p.hi: Prov. 10: 22. The blessing of the Lord maketh rich.
303. Need we not work for our daily bread when we pray for it every day?

div.p: Yes; God wants us to be diligent, each in our calling, trusting in His help.

p.hi: Gen. 3:19. In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread.
2 Thess. 3: 10. If any would not work, neither should he eat.

div.head: THE FIFTH PETITION.

p.hi: And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

div.p: That is,

We pray in this petition that our Father in heaven would not look upon our sins, nor, on account of them, deny our prayer; for we are not worthy of anything we ask, neither have we deserved it; but we pray that He would give it to us out of His mercy; for we sin every day, and deserve nothing but punishment.
And we on our part will heartily forgive those who have sinned against us, and return good for evil.

p.hi: 304. What do you pray for in the fifth petition?

div.p: I pray God to forgive us our trespasses.

p.hi: 305. What is implied by the word "trespasses"?

div.p: Thereby is implied our guilt or debt to God, which we have brought upon ourselves by our sins.

p.hi: 306. Can we feel assured that God will forgive us this debt?

div.p: Yes; Jesus Christ has paid for all our sins.

p.hi: 307. Why must the believer ask the forgiveness of sins every day?

div.p: Because he sins every day, and is always in need of forgiveness.

p.hi: 308. What do we confess to God in this petition?

div.p: We confess that we are not worthy of the least of that which we ask, neither have we deserved it; but we pray that He would give it to us out of His mercy.

p.hi: 309. What do we promise God in this petition, while asking His forgiveness?

div.p: We promise to forgive those who trespass against us, and return good for evil.

p.hi: Luke 6:37. Condemn not, and ye shall not be condemned: forgive, and ye shall be forgiven.

div.head: THE SIXTH PETITION.

p.hi: And lead us not into temptation.

div.p: That is,

God indeed tempts no one, but we pray in this petition that He would guard and keep us from the devil, the world, and our own flesh, that we fall not, through their deceit, into unbelief, despair, or other sins; but we pray that although we be thus tempted, we may overcome the temptation, and remain victorious.

p.hi: 310. What do you pray for in this petition?

div.p: I pray God not to lead us into temptation.

p.hi: 311. What is meant by temptation?

div.p: By temptation is meant opportunities that invite to sin.

p.hi: 312. Does God give us such opportunities in order that we may sin?

div.p: By no means; God, who is holy and loving, does not tempt any one to sin.

p.hi: James 1:13. Let no man say when he is tempted, I am tempted of God: for God cannot be tempted with evil, neither tempteth he any man.
313. Why then does God permit us to be tempted?

div.p: God permits us to be tempted in order to try us, and in order that it may be seen whether we have true faith, love, and patience.

p.hi: Read Gen. 22:1–19.
314. Who, on the other hand, tempt us to sin?

div.p: The devil, the world, and our own flesh, tempt us to sin.

p.hi: 315. How does the devil tempt us?

div.p: The devil tempts us by putting evil thoughts into our minds.

p.hi: 316. How does the world tempt us?

div.p: The world tempts us by threats, attractive invitations, and bad example.

p.hi: Prov. 1:10. My son if sinners entice thee, consent thou not.
317. How does our flesh tempt us?

div.p: Our own flesh tempts by its evil desires.

p.hi: James 1:14. Every man is tempted when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.
318. Can we ever be free from temptations in this world?

div.p: No; the conditions of this present life are such that temptations must follow, and we need them for our bringing up in the kingdom of God.

p.hi: Matt. 18:7. It must needs be that offences come.
319. What, then, do we mean when we ask God not to lead us into temptation?

div.p: We pray that when He finds it good for us to be tempted, He will guard and keep us, so that we may in the end be victorious.

p.hi: 1 Cor. 10:13. God is faithful who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able.
320. What are our weapons against temptation?

div.p: We must use the Word of God, watch and pray, and take care not to invite temptation.

p.hi: Matt. 26:41. Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation.
Eph. 6:13. Take unto you the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to withstand in the evil day, and having done all, to stand.

div.head: THE SEVENTH PETITION.

p.hi: But deliver us from evil.

div.p: That is,

We pray in this petition, in general, that our Father in heaven would deliver us from all evil, affecting body and soul, property and honor, and at last grant us a blessed end, and graciously take us from this world of sorrow to Himself in heaven.

p.hi: 321. What do you pray for in the seventh petition?

div.p: I pray God to deliver us from evil.

p.hi: 322. From what evil do you pray God to deliver us in this petition?

div.p: I pray God to deliver us from all sin that still clings to us, and from all the destructive effects of sin upon soul and body, property and honor.

p.hi: 323. Can we expect to be entirely free from all evil while in this world?

div.p: No, we cannot; but we pray God in this petition to deliver us more and more from all evil, and at last grant us a blessed end, and graciously take us from this world of sorrow to Himself in heaven.

p.hi: Phil. 1:23. I have a desire to depart, and to be with Christ; which is far better.
324. What are the closing words of the Lord's Prayer?
For Thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever and ever. Amen.
325. Of what do these words remind us?

div.p: We should remember that God is able to answer our prayer, and that the glory belongs to Him alone, when we get according to our prayer.

p.hi: 326. What is the meaning of the word "Amen"?

div.p: Its meaning is, Surely; so be it.

p.hi: 327. Why is this word added?

div.p: It is added in order that I may be fully assured that these petitions are acceptable to our Father in heaven, and are heard by Him.

p.hi: 328. How can I feel assured of this?

div.p: God Himself has commanded us to pray, and has added this promise to hear us: Amen, Amen; that is, Surely; so be it.

p.hi: 329. Does this promise hold good only when we use the Lord's Prayer?

div.p: No; God hears every prayer offered up according to His will.

p.hi: Matt. 7:7. Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you.
330. Does God always answer our prayer as we desire?

div.p: No; He often answers our prayer by giving us something else and something better than we ask or think.

p.hi: Eph. 3:20. God is able to do exceeding abundantly above all that we ask or think.
331. Does God answer our prayer at once?

div.p: Sometimes; but He often delays His answer in order to strengthen our faith and our hope.

p.hi: 332. In speaking with God, should we only ask for the good things which we like to get?

div.p: No; we must also return Him thanks for the blessings which we have received.

p.hi: Eph. 5: 20. Giving thanks always for all things unto God and the Father in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.

div.head: THE SACRAMENTS.

p.hi: 333. What is a sacrament?

div.p: A sacrament is a holy ordinance made by God Himself, in which He gives and confirms His invisible grace through outward and visible means.

p.hi: 334. Which are the sacraments of the Christian church?

div.p: They are Baptism and the Lord's Supper.

div.head: THE SACRAMENT OF BAPTISM.

p.hi: 335. What is Baptism?

div.p: Baptism is not water alone, but it is water comprehended in God's command, and united with His Word.

p.hi: 336. What is God's command concerning Baptism?

div.p: It is given in the words of Christ in the last chapter of Matthew:

"All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth. Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost: teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and, lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world."

p.hi: 337. In whose name then are you baptized?

div.p: I am baptized in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost.

p.hi: 338. Explain this further.

div.p: In Baptism I have entered into fellowship with the triune God, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost; I have become His own, and have been made heir of all His gracious gifts.

p.hi: 339. Is the baptism of little children in agreement with Christ's command?

div.p: Yes; Christ Himself has said: "Suffer the little children to come unto me, and forbid them not: for of such is the kingdom of God."

p.hi: Mark 10:14. John 3:5.
340. Who should administer Baptism?

div.p: Baptism should be administered by the minister of the church, but when necessary it may be administered by any Christian.

p.hi: 341. What benefit do we have from Baptism?

div.p: Baptism works the forgiveness of sins, delivers from death and the devil, and gives everlasting life to all who believe what the Word and promise of God declare.

p.hi: 342. What is God's promise concerning Baptism?

div.p: It is given in the words of Christ in the sixteenth chapter of Mark:
"He that believeth and is baptized shall be saved; but he that believeth not shall be condemned."

p.hi: 343. How does Baptism save us from sin, death, and the devil?

div.p: In Baptism we come into fellowship with Christ, and are made partakers in His redemption.

p.hi: Gal. 3:27. As many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ.
344. How can water do such great things?

div.p: It is not water indeed that does it, but the Word of God, which is in and with the water, and faith which trusts this Word of God in the water.
For without the Word of God, the water is water alone, and no Baptism. But with the Word of God it is a Baptism, that is, a gracious water of life and a washing of regeneration in the Holy Ghost.

p.hi: Titus 3:5–7. According to His mercy He saved us, by the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Holy Ghost;
Which He shed on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Savior;
That being justified by his grace, we should be made heirs according to the hope of eternal life.
345. Why is Baptism called the "washing of regeneration"?

div.p: Because the Holy Spirit in Baptism cleanses us from sin, and gives us a new spiritual life.

p.hi: 1 Pet. 3:21. Baptism is not the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but the answer of a good conscience toward God, by the resurrection of Jesus Christ.
346. Is not Baptism also called a covenant?

div.p: Yes; Baptism is a covenant; in Baptism God gives us a new life and His grace, and we promise Him to renounce the devil, and all His works, and all his ways, and to believe in the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.

p.hi: 347. Who enjoy the blessings that God promises in Baptism?

div.p: All who remain in the covenant of their Baptism.

p.hi: 348. When does he who was baptized as a child confirm the covenant of his Baptism?

div.p: At his confirmation, when he renews the covenant of his Baptism in the midst of the assembled congregation, having first been instructed in God's Word.

p.hi: 349. Is it possible to remain in the covenant of Baptism?

div.p: Yes; by the grace of God it is possible.

p.hi: Phil. 4:13. I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.
350. What must we do to remain in the grace of our Baptism?

div.p: We must watch and pray, and make diligent use of the Word of God and the Lord's Supper.

p.hi: 351. In what ways may we break the covenant of our Baptism?

div.p: 1. When we little by little forget our covenant, resist the Holy Spirit, and neglect prayer, so that we become more and more worldly-minded.
2. When we fall in coarse and open sins.

p.hi: 352. Will not God again receive us when we have broken the covenant of our Baptism?

div.p: Yes; God has not broken His part of the covenant, and when we again turn to Him, He is always glad to receive us.

p.hi: Luke 15:20. He arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.
353. How does a repentant sinner get courage to return to God?

div.p: He gets courage from considering the tender Gospel invitation of Christ, and from seeking God in prayer.

p.hi: Matt. 11:28. Come unto me, all that labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
354. Does not also he who remains true to the covenant of his Baptism need repentance?

div.p: Yes; he needs daily repentance and daily renewal. See 250.

p.hi: 355. What does the baptizing with water signify?

div.p: It signifies that the old man in us should, by daily sorrow and repentance, be drowned and die, with all sins and evil desires; and again a new man daily appear more and more, who shall live before God in righteousness and purity forever.

p.hi: 356. What is meant by saying that the old man in us should die, and the new man appear more and more?

div.p: Sin should be rooted out from us through daily sorrow and repentance, and our love to God and man should grow up within us more and more, so that it may appear in all our conduct that we have the mind of Christ.

p.hi: Rom. 6:4. We are buried with Christ by baptism into death: that like as Christ was raised up from the dead by the glory of the Father, even so we also should walk in newness of life.
357. What are the duties of sponsors?

div.p: They should pray for the child whose baptism they have witnessed, they should remember the covenant of their own Baptism, and afterwards, as far as possible, see that the child is brought up in the fear of God.

div.head: THE SACRAMENT OF THE LORD'S SUPPER.

p.hi: 358. What is the Lord's Supper?

div.p: It is the true body and blood of our Lord Jesus Christ, under bread and wine, instituted by Christ Himself for Christians to eat and to drink.

p.hi: 359. Repeat the Words of Institution.

div.p: "Our Lord Jesus Christ, in the night in which He was betrayed, took bread, and when He had given thanks, He brake it and gave it to his disciples, saying, Take, eat; this is my body, which is given for you; this do in remembrance of me.

"After the same manner, also, when He had supped, He took the cup, and when He had given thanks, He gave it to them, saying, Drink ye all of it; this cup is the New Testament in my blood, which is shed for you, and for many, for the remission of sins; this do, as oft as ye drink it, in remembrance of me."

p.hi: 360. When did Jesus institute the Lord's Supper?

div.p: In the night in which He was betrayed to death; it is therefore called the Lord's Supper.

p.hi: 361. Is it important to note the time when Jesus instituted the Lord's Supper?

div.p: Yes; for it shows the loving care of our Savior, who just before His suffering and death thought more of us than of Himself.

p.hi: 362. What do we receive in the Lord's Supper?

div.p: In and with the bread and the wine we receive the body and blood of Christ, which He gave up in death for us.

p.hi: 363. How do you know this?

div.p: Christ says concerning the bread: "Take, eat; this is my body."
Concerning the wine He says: "Drink ye all of it; this cup is the New Testament in my blood."

p.hi: 364. What is meant by "New Testament" in this connection?

div.p: Thereby is meant the new covenant which God has made and sealed with the blood of Jesus.

p.hi: 1 Cor. 10:16. The cup of blessing which we bless, is it not the communion of the blood of Christ? The bread which we break, is it not the communion of the body of Christ?
365. What, therefore, makes the bread and the wine a sacrament of the body and blood of Christ?

div.p: God's own Word which is added to the bread and the wine; for as Luther says, "Bread and wine alone are but bread and wine; but being united with the Word of God, they are truly the body and blood of Christ. For as the mouth of Christ speaks, so it is; He can neither lie nor deceive."

p.hi: 366. For whom is the Lord's Supper intended?

div.p: The Lord's Supper is intended for true Christians, who are of age and understanding to prove themselves.

p.hi: 1 Cor. 11: 28. [R. V.] Let a man prove himself, and so let him eat of the bread, and drink of the cup.
367. What benefit do we have from the Lord's Supper?

div.p: It is shown by these words: "Given and shed for you, for the remission of sins;" namely, that in the sacrament forgiveness of sins, life, and salvation are given us through these words. For where there is forgiveness of sins, there is also life and salvation.

p.hi: 368. But does not the believer have the forgiveness of sins before he partakes of the Lord's Supper?

div.p: Yes; the believer has the forgiveness of sins through Baptism and the Word.

p.hi: 369. How, then, can the forgiveness of sins in a particular sense be connected with this sacrament?

div.p: Because in the Lord's Supper we receive the body and blood of Christ, which were offered up for us, as a sure pledge of the forgiveness of sins.

p.hi: 370. In what way does the believer get life and salvation through this sacrament?

div.p: Through this sacrament the believer is brought into spiritual fellowship with his Lord and Savior, who imparts Himself to him and thus preserves and strengthens him in faith, hope, and love unto eternal life.

p.hi: John 6: 56. He that eateth my flesh, and drinketh my blood, dwelleth in me, and I in him.
371. Does not the sacrament of the Lord's Supper also bring about a more intimate fellowship between believers?

div.p: Yes; believers are united in a closer fellowship through partaking in common of the Lord Jesus and eternal life in Him.

p.hi: 1 Cor. 10:17. For we being many are one bread, and one body: for we are all partakers of that one bread.
372. How can bodily eating and drinking do such great things?

div.p: It is not the eating and drinking, indeed, that does it, but the words which stand here: "Given and shed for you, for the remission of sins." These words, together with the bodily eating and drinking, are the chief thing in the sacrament; and He that believes these words, has what they say and mean, namely, the forgiveness of sins.

p.hi: 373. Is it of little importance how we receive the Lord's Supper?

div.p: By no means; we must be prepared when we go to partake of these gifts. It is much worse to go to the Lord's Supper unprepared and unworthily than not to go at all.

p.hi: 374. Who, then, receive this sacrament worthily?

div.p: Fasting and bodily preparation are indeed a good outward practise;
But he alone is truly worthy and well prepared, who believes these words: "Given and shed for you, for the remission of sins."
But he who believes not these words is unworthy and unprepared. The words, "for you" require truly believing hearts.

p.hi: 375. Who, then, is rightly prepared to partake of the Lord's Supper?

div.p: He who believes these words: "Given and shed for you, for the remission of sins."

p.hi: 376. What is meant by "believing" these words?

div.p: Thereby is meant that we heartily feel our sin and unworthiness before God, but also that we confidently accept for ourselves the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ.

p.hi: 377. Who partake of the Lord's Supper unworthily?

div.p: They who do not feel nor repent their sins, and who do not from their heart believe in Jesus.

p.hi: 1 Cor. 11:29. He that eateth and drinketh unworthily, eateth and drinketh judgment to himself, not discerning the Lord's body.
378. Why do such unconverted persons partake of the Lord's Supper?

div.p: They do so either from custom or habit, or because they are ashamed to neglect the Lord's Supper, or again because they mean to please God by this outward obedience.

p.hi: 379. Should such persons be admitted to the Lord's Supper?

div.p: No.

p.hi: Matt 7:6. Give not that which is holy unto the dogs, neither cast ye your pearls before swine.
380. What must we do in order that we may not partake of the Lord's Supper unworthily?

div.p: We must prayerfully search our own hearts as in the presence of God, whether we repent our sins and believe in Jesus Christ, and whether we have an honest purpose to abstain from even our bosom sins.

p.hi: 381. How often should we partake of the Lord's Supper?

div.p: Christ has not told us how often we should partake, but He has said, "This do, as often as ye drink it, in remembrance of me".

p.hi: 382. What should move us to partake of the Lord's Supper often?

div.p: First of all, the command and promise of our Lord and Savior; then, our own great need, which is the reason for our Father's tender invitation and promise of grace.

p.hi: 383. What are the common causes for the neglect of the Lord's Supper?

div.p: Spiritual dullness and indifference, a worldly mind, pride, and disregard for God's grace and ordinance.

p.hi: 384. Should the feeling of our own unworthiness keep us away from the Lord's Supper?

div.p: No; the more we feel our own unworthiness, and the more we sincerely long for God's forgiveness, the more worthy are we to receive His grace.

p.hi: Matt. 5:3. Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
1 Pet. 5:5. God giveth grace to the humble.
385. What must we do when we receive the Lord's Supper?

div.p: We must remember our Savior and His death.

p.hi: Luke 22:19. This do in remembrance of me.
386. How should we remember Christ's death?

div.p: We should earnestly fix our mind upon the suffering and death of Christ, so that we may be strengthened in faith and in love to Him, who loved us unto death.

p.hi: 1 Cor. 11:26. As often as ye eat this bread, and drink this cup, ye do show the Lord's death till He come.
387. What should be our conduct when we have received the Lord's Supper?

div.p: We should quietly think of the great love which God has shown us, and heartily thank Him for it; not only for a few days, but always, keep near to Jesus, show His death in word and act, and in a sanctified life prove that the body and blood of Christ have power to cleanse from sin.

p.hi: 1 Pet. 2:24. Who his own self bore our sins in his own body on the tree, that we, being dead to sins, should live unto rigtheousness: by whose stripes ye were healed.
388. Is he who thus believes and lives in fellowship with Christ sure to be saved?

div.p: Yes; when he continues steadfast in faith until death.

p.hi: Matt. 24:13. He that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved.
Rev. 2:10. Be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life.
